steps.text: That's odd — a file named with an .md extension but saved as a .ps1 script into the Temp folder. That mismatch between file type and extension looks suspicious, so I want to look at what process initiated this download.

steps.text: This looks malicious — bitsadmin downloading a remote file disguised as a markdown but saved as .ps1 into Temp, run interactively at high integrity with no legitimate IT management parent process to justify it. The naming disguise is a strong indicator of intent to evade detection rather than a benign deployment scenario.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user wardog opened an interactive cmd.exe (proc-29da349e7e) at High integrity and ran bitsadmin.exe (proc-826bdb1e01) to start a foreground BITS transfer. The job pulled https://files.example-cdn.net/it-tools/main/docs/transfer.md and saved it as C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\update_check.ps1. That is a remote file disguised as a document, stored as a PowerShell script with an update-sounding name in the user's Temp folder. This fits ingress tool transfer through BITS (T1197/T1105). No management, update or deployment software launched it: the parent is a bare command prompt. The graph has no file or network-connection record for the download, so I couldn't confirm the script landed or ran. Response: isolate the host, delete the staged script, block the download domain, rotate wardog's credentials, and check for leftover BITS jobs.
